subject: Measurement invariance with mixed model with dichotomous and continous variables in constructs

messages.author: a9b1fc17ce131310
messages.subject: Measurement invariance with mixed model with dichotomous and continous variables in constructs
parts:
I have a question concerning measuring invariance and the obtained results in the case of mixed continuous-dichotomous model. If this group is not the right one, please suggest me where to raise that question.

 

 

My model has an endogenous latent variable composed of 5 dichotomous measured variables in one constructs, other constructs have it. Therefore, I used parameter ‘ordered’ inside cfa/sem functions. The (simplified) model was tested two years ago and it fits well.

 Now we gathered data in three countries, and we want to do multi-group comparison of SEM.


I’m using the complete dataset and lavaan 0.6-6.


When testing measurement invariance, the CFI for the configural model is worse than for the model with fixed loadings. In papers I found, the CFI of configural model was always higher than that for the model of metric invariance (while RMSEA is better - lower).

 Do you have any suggestion what to do/check? Could be a reason that I have both dichotomous and continuous variables of the model?

Or, stated differently, can the model be justified as acceptable one? 


I also run a permutation test, based on 1000 repetitions, revealed no evidence against the H0 of configural invariance using either.  (p = 0.285), CFI (p = 0.568), or RMSEA (p = 0.285) as criterion.

(I know that in this reported model below, the CFI for configural model (0.90) is borderline, but the same pattern is obtained if I check a model with a single construct.)

 

 


measurementInvariance(model=myModelCFA4,data=data.frame(dataMcc),ordered=c("Q40a", "Q40b", "Q40c", "Q40d","Q40e"), "group="Country",parameterization = "theta")


Measurement invariance models:
 

Model 1 : fit.configural

Model 2 : fit.loadings

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance with mixed model with dichotomous and continous variables in constructs
parts:
measurementInvariance() is designed only for continuous indicators, and measurementInvarianceCat() is designed only for ordered indicators.  Both functions are deprecated in semTools, in favor of using a more general function that can accommodate mixtures of items with different scales of measurement.  See the help page of ?measEq.syntax for an example of how to deal with binary items.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance with mixed model with dichotomous and continous variables in constructs
parts: What would be your suggestion when reporting model statistics: only Chisq scaled, only Chisq or both?
For each individual model, report its robust (scaled and shifted) test.  Likewise, when comparing models, report the robust chi-squared difference test.
